items.title: NGINX2Root: Five RCE bugs in NGINX, a Linux kernel path to root, and how to detect exploitation
Runtime security for Amazon EKS Auto Mode with Sysdig
items.description: Sysdig integrates with Amazon EKS Auto Mode hands node management to AWS, giving you immutable, Bottlerocket-based nodes with read-only root filesystems and no kernel module loading. But the shared responsibility model still applies: what happens inside your workloads at runtime is on you. This post explains how Sysdig Secure uses Universal eBPF and Falco-powered detection to deliver real-time runtime security on EKS Auto Mode. It covers deploying Host Shield, following nodes as AWS adds and replaces them, and catching threats with full Kubernetes context that static scanning alone can miss.

items.description: PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) lets an unauthenticated attacker run code on a PHP server with HTTP requests alone. The Sysdig Threat Research Team analyzed the exploitation and outlines affected versions, mitigations, and how to detect post-exploitation activity at runtime with Sysdig Secure and open source Falco.

items.description: An AI agent once deleted someone's entire inbox despite being told to confirm first. Not because it was malicious, but because the instruction didn't survive context compaction.
